summary.title: SimWAM: A Simple World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

details: Existing driving world-action models follow an 'imagine-then-act' pipeline that conditions the planner on generated future frames, placing costly video synthesis inside the real-time planning loop.
Goal: retain the benefit of video-dynamics priors while eliminating test-time future imagination.

SimWAM: a pretrained video-generation DiT (video expert) co-trained with a lightweight action DiT via joint flow matching over future-frame latents and ego trajectories; the two experts share no parameters and interact only through a shared attention stream.

Crux: an isolated attention mask lets both future-frame tokens and action tokens attend only to the current-observation latents and not to each other, so future-video prediction acts purely as training-time supervision and inference predicts trajectories directly without generating frames.
A subsequent RL stage converts the deterministic flow ODE into a marginal-preserving SDE and applies GRPO with a compositional driving reward to the action expert (LoRA-only updates).
NAVSIM (OpenScene/nuPlan): trained on navtrain (103,288 scenes), evaluated on navtest (12,146 scenes); primary metric PDMS combining NC, DAC, EP, TTC, Comfort.
Zero-shot transfer evaluated on nuScenes open-loop planning (L2, collision rate) with no fine-tuning or auxiliary annotations.
Input is a single front camera at 384x672 plus ego state (velocity, acceleration, yaw rate) and navigation command via T5 cross-attention.
Video expert initialized from Wan2.2-5B with its video VAE and T5 encoder; action expert is a DiT with hidden size 1024 (1.02B default).
Predicts 8 waypoints over 4 s at 2 Hz; video expert predicts the corresponding 8 future frames; joint loss with lambda=1.
Imitation stage: AdamW, cosine schedule, lr 1e-4, 100 epochs; inference uses 10 flow sampling steps.
Flow-GRPO-style SDE sampling with G=8 candidate trajectories per scenario, reward = NAVSIM PDM score, group-relative advantages with clipped update.
Only rank-32 LoRA adapters (alpha=16) on attention projections of the action expert are updated; lr 5e-5.
Training restricted to hard navtrain scenes where the imitation policy scores PDMS below 90.

Traditional E2E planners (UniAD, TransFuser, DiffusionDrive, WoTE, SeerDrive), VLM/VLA planners (AutoVLA, ReCogDrive, ExploreVLA, SGDrive, DriveVLA-W0), and world-model planners (Epona, DriveLaW, DriveWAM, PWM).
nuScenes zero-shot comparison against DriveVA and DriveWAM plus fine-tuned camera baselines.
Attention mask pattern (isolated vs bidirectional vs action-to-video), stage-wise components (action-only / +video / +RL).
Video backbone swaps (LTX-Video, Wan2.1-1.3B, Cosmos-Predict2.5, Wan2.2-5B) and action DiT scaling (0.21B/0.45B/1.02B).
Future-video target horizon/density, input resolution, sampling steps (with latency on a single A100), and exploration sampler (SDE vs random noise).

key_findings.finding: Future-video prediction used only as training-time supervision yields state-of-the-art planning while avoiding test-time future generation.
key_findings.evidence: SimWAM reaches 91.5 PDMS on NAVSIM navtest with a single front camera, exceeding world-model planners DriveWAM (90.1) and DriveLaW (89.1) and the best VLM planner SGDrive (91.1), with substantially lower latency than imagine-then-act world-model planners.

key_findings.finding: Blocking action tokens from attending to future-frame tokens costs nothing in accuracy relative to letting them see the imagined future.
key_findings.evidence: With imitation training only, the isolated mask attains 90.3 PDMS versus 90.2 for bidirectional and 90.1 for action-to-video attention, while additionally allowing the future-frame branch to be discarded at inference.

key_findings.finding: Video co-training and RL contribute large, complementary gains over a plain action-only diffusion planner.
key_findings.evidence: Action-only DiT scores 86.6 PDMS; adding the video expert raises it to 90.3 (improving all submetrics); adding GRPO RL raises it to 91.5, mainly through DAC (98.7) and EP (86.4), for a total +4.9 points.

key_findings.finding: The decoupled two-expert interface makes the video backbone swappable and the action expert independently scalable.
key_findings.evidence: Swapping backbones gives 88.7 (LTX-Video), 90.2 (Wan2.1-1.3B), 90.3 (Wan2.2-5B), 90.4 (driving-pretrained Cosmos-Predict2.5) PDMS with no other changes; scaling the action DiT from 0.21B to 1.02B improves PDMS from 89.9 to 90.3.

key_findings.finding: RL is most effective when restricted to hard scenes and when exploration uses the marginal-preserving SDE rather than random noise injection.
key_findings.evidence: Training on the sub-90-PDMS navtrain subset consistently beats full-set RL, peaking at 91.5 PDMS at 15k steps before declining; the SDE sampler gives 91.5 PDMS with NC 98.4 / TTC 95.5 versus 91.3 with NC 97.7 / TTC 94.1 for random-noise exploration.
